import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
np.random.seed(361)
df = pd.DataFrame(np.random.randint(0,3,(30,4)), columns=['A','B','C','D'])
def run_lengths(s):
    lens = []
    prev = None
    count = 0
    for v in s:
        if v==prev:
            count += 1
        else:
            if prev is not None:
                lens.append(count)
            count = 1
            prev = v
    lens.append(count)
    return pd.Series(lens)
for c in df.columns:
    rl = run_lengths(df[c])
    plt.plot(rl, label=c)
plt.legend()
plt.title('Run Lengths Per Feature')
plt.show()

import networkx as nx

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
def mad_outlier(series):
  med = series.median()
  mad = np.median(np.abs(series-med))
  return np.abs(series-med)>(3*mad)

df['outlier'] = mad_outlier(df['val'])

from transformers import DistilBertTokenizerFast, DistilBertForSequenceClassification, Trainer, TrainingArguments
import torch
import pandas as pd
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/clmentb/gender-classifier-dataset
df = pd.read_csv('gender-classifier.csv').head(28)
tokenizer = DistilBertTokenizerFast.from_pretrained('distilbert-base-uncased')
texts = df['text'].fillna('').tolist()
y = df['gender'].factorize()[0]
encodings = tokenizer(texts, truncation=True, padding=True)
class MyDataset(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
    def __init__(self, encodings, labels): self.encodings, self.labels = encodings, labels
    def __getitem__(self, i):
        item = {k: torch.tensor(v[i]) for k, v in self.encodings.items()}
        item['labels'] = torch.tensor(self.labels[i]); return item
    def __len__(self): return len(self.labels)
dataset = MyDataset(encodings, y)
model = DistilBertForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained('distilbert-base-uncased', num_labels=len(set(y)))
args = TrainingArguments(output_dir='./out', per_device_train_batch_size=4, num_train_epochs=1)
Trainer(model=model, train_dataset=dataset, args=args).train()

import pandas as pd

def is_fib(n):
    a,b=0,1
    while b<=n:
        if b==n: return True
        a,b=b,a+b
    return False

df = pd.DataFrame({'num': range(0, 25)})
df['is_fibonacci'] = df['num'].map(is_fib)

import pandas as pd

def middle_chars(s):
    if len(s)<2:
        return ''
    mid = len(s)//2
    return s[mid-1:mid+2] if len(s)%2==1 else s[mid-1:mid+1]
df['middle_chars'] = df['word'].map(middle_chars)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.model_selection import KFold
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score
X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)
kf = KFold(n_splits=4)
roc_scores = []
for train, test in kf.split(X):
    model = LogisticRegression()
    model.fit(X[train], y[train])
    prob = model.predict_proba(X[test])
    base_roc = roc_auc_score(y[test], prob, multi_class='ovr')
    roc_scores.append(base_roc)
plt.plot(roc_scores, marker='o')
plt.show()

from transformers import XLNetTokenizer, XLNetForSequenceClassification, TrainingArguments, Trainer
import pandas as pd
import torch
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/msambare/amazon-employee-access-challenge
train = pd.read_csv('train.csv').sample(n=90, random_state=3)
texts = train['RESOURCE'].astype(str).tolist()
labels = train['ROLE_CODE'].astype('category').cat.codes.values
tokenizer = XLNetTokenizer.from_pretrained('xlnet-base-cased')
enc = tokenizer(texts, truncation=True, padding=True, return_tensors='pt')
model = XLNetForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained('xlnet-base-cased', num_labels=len(np.unique(labels)))
class Dataset(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
    def __init__(self, enc, labels): self.enc=enc; self.labels=labels
    def __getitem__(self, i): return {**{k:v[i] for k,v in self.enc.items()}, 'labels': torch.tensor(self.labels[i])}
    def __len__(self): return len(self.labels)
data = Dataset(enc, labels)
args = TrainingArguments('test_mdl', num_train_epochs=1, per_device_train_batch_size=8)
Trainer(model, args, train_dataset=data).train()

from transformers import GPT2Tokenizer, GPT2ForSequenceClassification, Trainer, TrainingArguments
import pandas as pd
import torch
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/clmentbisaillon/fake-and-real-news-dataset
train = pd.read_csv('Fake.csv').sample(50)

class Dataset(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
    def __init__(self, enc, labels): self.enc=enc; self.labels=labels
    def __getitem__(self, i): return {**{k:v[i] for k,v in self.enc.items()}, 'labels': torch.tensor(self.labels[i])}
    def __len__(self): return len(self.labels)
dataset = Dataset(tok, labels)
args = TrainingArguments('out_gpt2', num_train_epochs=1, per_device_train_batch_size=3)
Trainer(model, args, train_dataset=dataset).train()

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
from transformers import pipeline
from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix
import numpy as np
texts = ["Positive review.", "Negative feedback.", "Neutral statement.", "Love it!", "Not my favorite."]

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
from datasets import Dataset
import torch
import numpy as np
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('distilbert-base-uncased')
texts = ['this is great', 'terrible experience', 'it was okay', 'loved it', 'disliked the service']
labels = [1, 0, 1, 1, 0]
dset = Dataset.from_dict({'text': texts, 'label': labels})
def preprocess(example):
    return tokenizer(example['text'], truncation=True, padding='max_length', max_length=32)
dset = dset.map(preprocess, batched=True)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained('distilbert-base-uncased', num_labels=2)
loader = DataLoader(dset.with_format('torch'), batch_size=2)
optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=3e-5)
for epoch in range(3):
    for batch in loader:
        model.train()
        out = model(input_ids=batch['input_ids'], attention_mask=batch['attention_mask'], labels=batch['label'])
        out.loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        optimizer.zero_grad()
model.eval()
all_preds = []
for batch in loader:
    logits = model(input_ids=batch['input_ids'], attention_mask=batch['attention_mask']).logits
    all_preds.extend(np.argmax(logits.detach().numpy(), axis=1))
acc = np.mean(np.array(all_preds) == np.array(labels))
print('Accuracy:', acc)

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification
from datasets import Dataset
import torch
reviews = ['good food', 'bad service', 'excellent staff', 'poor hygiene', 'average']
y = [1,0,1,0,1]
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('distilbert-base-uncased')
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained('distilbert-base-uncased', num_labels=2)
def preprocess(ex):
    return tokenizer(ex['review'], truncation=True, padding='max_length', max_length=32)
dset = Dataset.from_dict({'review': reviews, 'label': y}).map(preprocess, batched=True)
loader = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(dset.with_format('torch'), batch_size=2)
optim = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=2e-5)
for e in range(2):
    for batch in loader:
        model.train()
        out = model(input_ids=batch['input_ids'], attention_mask=batch['attention_mask'], labels=batch['label'])
        out.loss.backward()
        optim.step()
        optim.zero_grad()
model.eval()
preds = []
for batch in loader:
    logits = model(input_ids=batch['input_ids'], attention_mask=batch['attention_mask']).logits
    preds += logits.argmax(dim=1).tolist()
acc = sum([a==b for a, b in zip(preds, y)])/len(y)
print('Fake review classifier accuracy:', acc)

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel
import torch
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2')
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained('sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2')
sentences = ["OpenAI makes AI.", "Transformers change NLP.", "Python is widely used."]
inputs = tokenizer(sentences, padding=True, truncation=True, return_tensors='pt')
with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(**inputs)
    embeddings = outputs.last_hidden_state.mean(dim=1).cpu().numpy()
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
reduced = pca.fit_transform(embeddings)
plt.scatter(reduced[:,0], reduced[:,1])
plt.xlabel("PC1")
plt.ylabel("PC2")
plt.title("PCA of Transformer Embeddings")
plt.show()

import pandas as pd
from collections import Counter

def ngram_freq(text, n=2):
    words = text.split()
    ngrams = zip(*[words[i:] for i in range(n)])
    return dict(Counter([' '.join(ng) for ng in ngrams]))

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
texts = ["cat dog dog cat dog", "dog cat mouse", "mouse mouse dog cat"]
df = pd.DataFrame({'text': texts})
def entropy(row):
    w = row.split()
    p = np.array(list(pd.Series(w).value_counts(normalize=True)))
    return -(p * np.log2(p)).sum()
df['word_entropy'] = df['text'].apply(entropy)
print(df)

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from transformers import RobertaTokenizer, RobertaForSequenceClassification, Trainer, TrainingArguments
import torch
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/clmentbisaillon/fake-and-real-news-dataset

df = pd.read_csv('Fake.csv').sample(500)
tokens = RobertaTokenizer.from_pretrained('roberta-base')
class FakeNewsDataset(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
    def __init__(self, df, tokens, max_len=128):
        self.text = df['text'].tolist()
        self.labels = df['label'].map({'FAKE':0,'REAL':1}).tolist()
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.max_len = max_len
    def __len__(self): return len(self.text)
    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        encode = self.tokens(self.text[idx], truncation=True, padding='max_length', max_length=self.max_len, return_tensors='pt')
        return {key: val.squeeze() for key, val in encode.items()}, torch.tensor(self.labels[idx])
df['label'] = 'FAKE'
df_test = pd.read_csv('True.csv').sample(500)
df_test['label'] = 'REAL'
df_full = pd.concat([df, df_test]).reset_index(drop=True)
X_train, X_test = train_test_split(df_full, test_size=0.25, stratify=df_full['label'], random_state=7)
train_dataset = FakeNewsDataset(X_train, tokens)
test_dataset = FakeNewsDataset(X_test, tokens)
model = RobertaForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained('roberta-base', num_labels=2)
training_args = TrainingArguments(output_dir="./results", num_train_epochs=1, logging_steps=50, per_device_train_batch_size=8, per_device_eval_batch_size=8, evaluation_strategy="epoch", save_strategy="no", disable_tqdm=True)
trainer = Trainer(model=model, args=training_args, train_dataset=train_dataset, eval_dataset=test_dataset)
trainer.train()
trainer.evaluate()

    sentences = sent_tokenize(text)

import pandas as pd
import nltk
nltk.download('punkt')
nltk.download('averaged_perceptron_tagger')
def top_n_nouns(text, n=3):
    tokens = nltk.word_tokenize(text)
    pos = nltk.pos_tag(tokens)
    freq = {}
    for word, tag in pos:
        if tag.startswith('NN'):
            freq[word] = freq.get(word, 0) + 1
    return sorted(freq, key=lambda k: -freq[k])[:n]
df = pd.DataFrame({'text': ["The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. Dogs are popular pets."]})
df['top_nouns'] = df['text'].apply(lambda t: top_n_nouns(t, n=2))

def pos_count(text):
    sents = nltk.sent_tokenize(text)
    out = []
    for s in sents:
        tags = nltk.pos_tag(nltk.word_tokenize(s))
        counts = {}
        for _, tag in tags:
            counts[tag] = counts.get(tag, 0) + 1
        out.append(counts)
    return out

fpr = [0]
tpr = [0]
thresholds = np.linspace(0,1,50)
for th in thresholds:
    pred_th = proba > th
    fpr.append((pred_th & (y==0)).sum()/((y==0).sum()))
    tpr.append((pred_th & (y==1)).sum()/((y==1).sum()))

        self.rfc = RandomForestClassifier()
    def fit_grid(self, X, y):

from transformers import AutoModelForSequenceClassification, AutoTokenizer, Trainer, TrainingArguments
import pandas as pd
import torch
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/clmentbison/amazon-product-review
reviews = pd.read_csv('amazon_reviews.csv')
X, y = reviews['review'], reviews['category']
X_train, X_eval, y_train, y_eval = train_test_split(X, y, random_state=0)
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased')
train_tok = tokenizer(list(X_train), truncation=True, padding=True)
eval_tok = tokenizer(list(X_eval), truncation=True, padding=True)
class Dataset(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
    def __init__(self, input_ids, attention_mask, labels):
        self.input_ids, self.attention_mask, self.labels = input_ids, attention_mask, labels
    def __len__(self): return len(self.labels)
    def __getitem__(self, idx): return {"input_ids": torch.tensor(self.input_ids[idx]), "attention_mask": torch.tensor(self.attention_mask[idx]), "labels": torch.tensor(self.labels[idx])}
train_ds = Dataset(train_tok['input_ids'], train_tok['attention_mask'], y_train.astype('category').cat.codes.tolist())
eval_ds = Dataset(eval_tok['input_ids'], eval_tok['attention_mask'], y_eval.astype('category').cat.codes.tolist())
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained('bert-base-uncased', num_labels=len(set(list(y))))
trainer = Trainer(model=model, train_dataset=train_ds, eval_dataset=eval_ds, args=TrainingArguments(output_dir='bert_out', num_train_epochs=1, per_device_train_batch_size=16, eval_steps=20))
trainer.train()

from transformers import AlbertTokenizer, AlbertForSequenceClassification, Trainer, TrainingArguments
import pandas as pd
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/benblakewin/musical-genre-classification
music = pd.read_csv('music_genre.csv')
X = music['text'].values.tolist()
y = music['genre'].astype('category').cat.codes.values.tolist()
tokenizer = AlbertTokenizer.from_pretrained('albert-base-v2')
tok = tokenizer(X, truncation=True, padding=True)
class DS:
    def __init__(self, ids, mask, labels):
        self.input_ids, self.attention_mask, self.labels = ids, mask, labels
    def __len__(self): return len(self.labels)
    def __getitem__(self, i): return {"input_ids": self.input_ids[i], "attention_mask": self.attention_mask[i], "labels": self.labels[i]}
ds = DS(tok['input_ids'], tok['attention_mask'], y)
model = AlbertForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained('albert-base-v2', num_labels=len(set(y)))
args = TrainingArguments(output_dir='albert_out', num_train_epochs=1)
Trainer(model=model, args=args, train_dataset=ds).train()

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification, Trainer, TrainingArguments
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/clmentbisaillon/ultrabrain-classification
texts = ['sample sentence 1', 'sentence for class 2', 'sentence for class 1']
labels = [0,1,0]
model_name = 'distilbert-base-uncased'
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(model_name, num_labels=2)
ds = [{'input_ids':tokenizer(t, truncation=True, padding='max_length', max_length=32)['input_ids'],'label':l} for t,l in zip(texts, labels)]
def collate(batch):
    return {
        'input_ids': np.array([b['input_ids'] for b in batch]),
        'labels': np.array([b['label'] for b in batch])
    }
args = TrainingArguments(output_dir='./tmp', per_device_train_batch_size=2, num_train_epochs=1)
trainer = Trainer(model=model, train_dataset=ds, args=args, data_collator=collate)
trainer.train()
preds = trainer.predict(ds).predictions
print(np.max(preds, axis=1))

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification, Trainer, TrainingArguments
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/abhinavk/onu-news-classification
import pandas as pd
texts = ['Fake news example', 'True statement']
labels = [0, 1]
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('bert-base-cased')
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained('bert-base-cased', num_labels=2)
enc = tokenizer(texts, padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=24, return_tensors='pt')
class SimpleDS:
    def __init__(self, enc, labels):
        self.enc = enc
        self.labels = labels
    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        o = {k:self.enc[k][idx] for k in self.enc}
        o['labels'] = self.labels[idx]
        return o
    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.labels)
ds = SimpleDS(enc, labels)
args = TrainingArguments(output_dir='./tmp', num_train_epochs=2, per_device_train_batch_size=2)
tr = Trainer(model, args, train_dataset=ds)
res = tr.train()
losses = res.history['loss']
print(losses[-1])

import pandas as pd

# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/crowdflower/twitter-airline-sentiment

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

def resize_and_pad(img_arr, target_size=128):
    h, w = img_arr.shape[:2]
    scale = target_size / max(h, w)
    resized = np.array(Image.fromarray(img_arr).resize((int(w*scale), int(h*scale))))
    pad_h = target_size - resized.shape[0]
    pad_w = target_size - resized.shape[1]
    pad = ((pad_h//2, pad_h - pad_h//2), (pad_w//2, pad_w - pad_w//2), (0, 0)) if resized.ndim == 3 else ((pad_h//2, pad_h - pad_h//2), (pad_w//2, pad_w - pad_w//2))
    out = np.pad(resized, pad, mode='constant', constant_values=0)
    return out
img = np.random.randint(0, 255, (64, 90, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
square_img = resize_and_pad(img, 128)

task_name: Apply Homomorphic Filtering on Grayscale Image
code:
import cv2
import numpy as np
img = cv2.imread('sample.jpg', 0)/255.0
log_img = np.log1p(img)
dft = np.fft.fft2(log_img)
rows, cols = img.shape
mask = np.ones((rows, cols))
center = (rows//2, cols//2)
for i in range(rows):
    for j in range(cols):
        mask[i,j] = 0.5 + 0.5 * np.exp(-((i-center[0])**2+(j-center[1])**2)/(2*30*30))
dft_filt = dft * mask
img_filt = np.abs(np.fft.ifft2(dft_filt))
img_out = np.expm1(img_filt)
cv2.imwrite('homomorphic_filtered.jpg', (img_out * 255).astype('uint8'))

ims = [np.random.randint(0,255,(np.random.randint(50,120),np.random.randint(50,120),3),dtype=np.uint8) for _ in range(5)]
def pad_to_multiple(im, mul=32):
    h,w = im.shape[:2]
    newh = ((h+mul-1)//mul)*mul
    neww = ((w+mul-1)//mul)*mul
    pad = np.zeros((newh,neww,3),dtype=im.dtype)
    pad[:h,:w]=im
    return pad

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.api as sm
np.random.seed(5)
length = 500
dt = np.arange(length)
series = np.sin(2*np.pi*dt/24) + np.sin(2*np.pi*dt/120) + np.random.normal(0,0.4,length)
df = pd.DataFrame({'timestamp': pd.date_range('2023-01-01', periods=length, freq='H'), 'ts': series})
lags = range(1,121)
autocorr = [df['ts'].autocorr(lag) for lag in lags]
plt.plot(lags, autocorr)
plt.xlabel('Lag')
plt.ylabel('Autocorrelation')
plt.title('Autocorrelation (Seasonality) Multi-period Series')
plt.show()

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
np.random.seed(8)
length = 2000

values = np.random.randn(length) + 2*np.sin(hours.hour/2)

window = 24
rmean = df.rolling(window).mean()
rstd = df.rolling(window).std()
plt.plot(df.index, df, alpha=0.3, label='value')

plt.plot(rstd.index, rstd, label='rolling std')
plt.legend()
plt.title('Hourly Series with Rolling Mean and Std')
plt.show()

import pandas as pd
from scipy.interpolate import UnivariateSpline
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
dates = pd.date_range('2023-06-01', periods=90, freq='D')
series = pd.Series(np.sin(np.linspace(0, 12, 90))+np.random.normal(0,0.3,90), index=dates)

series.iloc[nan_idx]=np.nan
x=np.arange(90)
y=series.values
mask=~np.isnan(y)
interp=UnivariateSpline(x[mask],y[mask],s=1)
y_filled=series.copy()
y_filled.iloc[np.isnan(y)] = interp(x[np.isnan(y)])
plt.hist(series.dropna(),alpha=0.6,label='Raw')
plt.hist(y_filled,alpha=0.4,label='Spline')
plt.legend()
plt.show()

                err = R[i,j]-np.dot(P[i,:],Q[j,:].T)

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from implicit.als import AlternatingLeastSquares
from scipy.sparse import csr_matrix
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/gabriellmb/tmall-users-shopping-log-dataset
log = pd.read_csv('tmall_users_shopping_log.csv')
user_ids, item_ids = log['user_id'].astype('category').cat.codes, log['item_id'].astype('category').cat.codes
matrix = csr_matrix((log['purchase_count'], (user_ids, item_ids)), shape=(user_ids.nunique(), item_ids.nunique()))
model = AlternatingLeastSquares(factors=32, regularization=0.05, iterations=10)
model.fit(matrix)
user = np.random.randint(matrix.shape[0])
top_items = model.recommend(user, matrix, N=10)
pd.DataFrame(top_items, columns=['item_id', 'score'])

from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/shazamapp/spotify-dataset
tracks = pd.read_csv('spotify_tracks.csv')
content = minmax_scale(tracks[['valence','acousticness']].sum(axis=1))
collab = minmax_scale(tracks['popularity'])
score = 0.6*content+0.4*collab
tracks['score']=score
tracks.sort_values('score',ascending=False).head(8)[['track_name','score']]

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jayvee94/food-item-recommendation-dataset
food = pd.read_csv('food_tags.csv')
X = StandardScaler().fit_transform(food[['calories', 'protein']])
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=1)
food['cluster'] = kmeans.fit_predict(X)
popscore = food.groupby('cluster')['calories'].mean()
recommend = food[food['cluster']==popscore.idxmax()].sort_values('calories',ascending=False).head(6)
recommend[['item_id','cluster']]

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.decomposition import TruncatedSVD
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/gabriellmb/tmall-users-shopping-log-dataset
log = pd.read_csv('tmall_users_shopping_log.csv')
user_c = log['user_id'].astype('category').cat.codes
item_c = log['item_id'].astype('category').cat.codes
mat = np.zeros((user_c.nunique(), item_c.nunique()))
mat[user_c, item_c] = log['purchase_count']
bias = mat.mean(axis=0)
svd = TruncatedSVD(n_components=7)
U = svd.fit_transform(mat) + bias
rec = pd.DataFrame({'item': np.arange(len(bias)), 'score': U[0]})
rec.sort_values('score',ascending=False).head(10)

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jayvee94/food-item-recommendation-dataset

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.preprocessing import MultiLabelBinarizer
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier

pred = knn.kneighbors([group_vec], return_distance=False)[0]

top = pred[np.argsort(blend)[-2:][::-1]]

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from transformers import pipeline
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/rounakbanik/the-movies-dataset
movies = pd.read_csv('movies.csv')
users = pd.read_csv('ratings.csv')
user_movies = users[users['userId']==25]['movieId'].values
movie_texts = movies[movies['movieId'].isin(user_movies)]['overview'].fillna('')
recommender = pipeline('feature-extraction', model='sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2')
embeddings = np.vstack([np.mean(np.array(recommender([t])[0]), axis=0) for t in movie_texts])
new_movies = movies[~movies['movieId'].isin(user_movies)].sample(20)
new_emb = [np.mean(np.array(recommender([t])[0]), axis=0) for t in new_movies['overview'].fillna('')]
sim = np.dot(np.array(new_emb), embeddings.T)
top_idx = np.argsort(sim.sum(axis=1))[::-1][:5]
print(new_movies.iloc[top_idx][['title']])

from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
np.random.seed(1)
x = np.random.randn(200)
y = 2.4 * x + np.random.normal(0, 2.5, size=x.shape)
df = pd.DataFrame({'feature_x': x, 'feature_y': y})
model = LinearRegression().fit(df[['feature_x']], df['feature_y'])
x_vals = np.linspace(df['feature_x'].min(), df['feature_x'].max(), 100)
pred = model.predict(x_vals.reshape(-1, 1))
yerr = np.std(df['feature_y'] - model.predict(df[['feature_x']]))
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
sns.scatterplot(data=df, x='feature_x', y='feature_y', alpha=0.4)
plt.plot(x_vals, pred, color='r')
plt.fill_between(x_vals, pred - yerr, pred + yerr, color='orange', alpha=0.2)
plt.title('Scatterplot w/ Regression and Confidence Band')
plt.show()

import pandas as pd
import torch
# DATASET USED: https://www.kaggle.com/c/jigsaw-toxic-comment-classification-challenge/data
train = pd.read_csv('train.csv')
texts = train['comment_text'].fillna('').values[:250]
labels = train[['toxic', 'severe_toxic', 'obscene', 'threat', 'insult', 'identity_hate']].values[:250]
tokenizer = DistilBertTokenizerFast.from_pretrained('distilbert-base-uncased')

model = DistilBertForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained('distilbert-base-uncased', num_labels=6)
class Dataset(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
    def __init__(self, encodings, labels): 
      self.encodings=encodings; self.labels=labels
    def __getitem__(self, i): 
      return {**{key:val[i] for key,val in self.encodings.items()}, 'labels': torch.tensor(self.labels[i], dtype=torch.float)}
    def __len__(self): 
      return len(self.labels)
dataset = Dataset(X_tok, labels)
args = TrainingArguments('test_output', num_train_epochs=1, per_device_train_batch_size=8, logging_steps=10)
trainer = Trainer(model=model, args=args, train_dataset=dataset)
trainer.train()

features = ['Feature1','Feature2','Feature3','Feature4','Feature5']
cats = ['X','Y','Z']
data = np.vstack([np.random.normal(i,0.5, (100, len(features))) for i in range(len(cats))])
df = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=features)
df['Category'] = np.repeat(cats, 100)
means = df.groupby('Category').mean()
angles = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, len(features), endpoint=False)
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(7,7))
ax = fig.add_subplot(111, polar=True)
for idx, cat in enumerate(means.index):
    vals = np.concatenate([means.loc[cat].values], [means.loc[cat].values[0]])
    ax.plot(np.concatenate([angles, [angles[0]]]), vals, label=cat)
ax.set_xticks(angles)
ax.set_xticklabels(features)
plt.title('Radar Chart of Means by Category')
plt.legend()
plt.show()
